title: What My Father Understood About Small Daily Signs
script: Narrator: [warmly] My father was a fisherman for almost forty years, and although he never studied religion formally, he understood Allah in a way few scholars ever explained to me.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Every morning before sailing out, he would stand quietly by the boat and look at the sky for several minutes.
Narrator: [reflective] As a boy, I once asked him what exactly he was looking for out there, since the sky looked ordinary to me.
Narrator: [gently] He said, I'm not just checking the weather, son. I'm remembering who arranged all of this so perfectly before I even woke up today.
Narrator: [warmly] I didn't fully understand him then, because I was young and mostly wanted breakfast, not philosophy, so early in the morning.
Narrator: [softly] Years later, after I moved to the city and started my own stressful office job, I began remembering his words more often.
Narrator: [thoughtful] During difficult weeks, when everything felt uncertain, I found myself standing by my window, doing the same quiet thing he used to do.
Narrator: [reflective] I noticed how the sunrise arrived at the exact same gentle pace every single morning, whether I was calm or completely anxious inside.
Narrator: [gently] That consistency started to comfort me, because it reminded me that some things remain perfectly ordered, even when my own life feels chaotic.
Narrator: [warmly] My father used to say that Allah doesn't only speak through miracles, He speaks constantly through patterns we've simply stopped noticing.
Narrator: [thoughtful] The tide that returns every day, the seasons that change on schedule, even a wound that quietly heals itself without our help.
Narrator: [peacefully] These aren't accidents happening randomly around us, he always insisted, they're quiet daily signs, if only we slow down enough to actually see them.
Narrator: [with feeling] My father passed away three years ago, but I still stand by windows sometimes, remembering how he watched the sky every single morning.
Narrator: [warmly] Now, when my own son asks what I'm doing standing there so quietly, I finally understand exactly what to tell him.
